description: Final 50-question reviewed set spanning all eight bundled document categories, including calendar distractors, multi-fact cases, policy and cost edge cases, and three deliberately unanswerable questions. Every answerable item was checked against its cited bundled source and evidence.

questions.question: When does Fall 2026 registration begin in eServices?
questions.expected_answer: Fall 2026 registration begins Monday, March 23, 2026.
questions.expected_evidence:
Monday, March 23, 2026
– Fall 2026 registration begins in eServices
questions.reviewer_notes: Distinguishes Fall 2026 from similar calendar documents.

questions.question: When does Spring 2026 registration begin?
questions.expected_answer: Spring 2026 registration begins Monday, October 20, 2025.
questions.expected_evidence:
Monday, October 20, 2025
– Spring 2026 registration begins in eServices

questions.question: On what date does Summer 2026 open registration for visiting students begin?
questions.expected_answer: Summer 2026 open registration begins Monday, April 6, 2026.
questions.expected_evidence:
Monday, April 6, 2026
– Summer 2026 OPEN (visiting students) registration begins in eServices

questions.question: How many transferable college-level semester credits make a student a transfer applicant?
questions.expected_answer: A student applies as a transfer applicant after attempting at least 16 transferable college-level semester credits.
questions.expected_evidence: Students who have attempted at least 16 transferable, college-level semester credits at another institution apply to Metro State as transfer students.

questions.question: What high school GPA qualifies a first-year applicant for automatic admission?
questions.expected_answer: Automatic first-year admission requires a cumulative high school GPA of 2.75 or higher.
questions.expected_evidence: Requires a cumulative high school GPA of 2.75 or higher

questions.question: Does the bookstore credit program give students free textbooks?
questions.expected_answer: No. It lets eligible students charge required materials to their student account, and they remain responsible for any balance not covered by aid.
questions.expected_evidence:
Charges are applied to the student account and covered by financial aid once disbursed
- Students are responsible for any remaining balance not covered by aid
accepted_answers: students are responsible for the remaining balance

questions.question: What expenses are included in Metro State's cost of attendance estimate?
questions.expected_answer: It includes tuition and mandatory fees, books and course materials, housing and food, transportation, personal expenses, and applicable loan fees.
questions.expected_evidence:
Typical cost categories:
- Tuition and mandatory fees
- Books and course materials
- Housing and food
- Transportation
- Personal expenses
- Loan fees (if applicable)
accepted_answers: tuition, books, housing, food, transportation, personal expenses, and loan fees

questions.question: What does last-dollar mean for the North Star Promise Scholarship?
questions.expected_answer: It covers remaining eligible tuition and fees after other federal and state grants have been applied.
questions.expected_evidence: It is a “last-dollar” scholarship, meaning it covers remaining tuition and fees after other federal and state grants have been applied.
accepted_answers: covers remaining tuition and fees after grants

questions.question: When does Return to Title IV review apply after a withdrawal?
questions.expected_answer: It applies when a student withdraws from all courses before completing more than 60 percent of the term.
questions.expected_evidence: Federal regulations require the university to review financial aid eligibility when a student withdraws before completing more than 60 percent of a term.
accepted_answers: before completing more than 60 percent of the term
withdraws from all courses before 60 percent

questions.question: What is the difference between graduation and commencement?
questions.expected_answer: Graduation officially confirms completion of degree requirements; commencement is an optional ceremony and does not itself confirm completion.
questions.expected_evidence: Graduation is the official confirmation that a student has completed all degree requirements. Completion is verified through the Degree Audit Report and processed by the Registrar’s Office.
accepted_answers: graduation confirms degree completion; commencement is the ceremony
questions.reviewer_notes: The cited source separately states that commencement is optional and does not indicate degree completion.

questions.question: When is Spring 2026 undergraduate and graduate commencement?
questions.expected_answer: Spring 2026 undergraduate and graduate commencement is Monday, May 4, 2026.
questions.expected_evidence:
Monday, May 4, 2026
Spring 2026 Undergraduate and Graduate Commencement

questions.question: Which grade is used in GPA calculations when a Metro State course is repeated?
questions.expected_answer: The most recent grade is used in the GPA calculation, although every attempt remains on the transcript.
questions.expected_evidence: The most recent grade is used in GPA calculations, although all attempts remain on the transcript.

questions.question: Does satisfactory academic progress affect financial aid eligibility?
questions.expected_answer: Yes. Students must meet GPA, completion-percentage, and maximum-timeframe standards to maintain financial aid eligibility.
questions.expected_evidence: SAP applies to financial aid eligibility. Students must meet GPA requirements, complete a minimum percentage of attempted credits, and finish their degree within the maximum timeframe.

questions.question: Which course delivery method has scheduled online video meetings?
questions.expected_answer: Online synchronous courses meet online at scheduled times using video conferencing.
questions.expected_evidence:
Online Synchronous
Courses meet online at scheduled times using video conferencing.

questions.question: What should students check in eServices before their registration window opens?
questions.expected_answer: They should check for registration holds and resolve them before the window opens.
questions.expected_evidence: Check for registration holds in eServices and resolve them before your window opens.

questions.question: What are the Fall 2026 term dates?
questions.expected_answer: The Fall 2026 term runs from August 22 through December 13, 2026.
questions.expected_evidence:
Fall 2026 Term Dates
- August 22, 2026 to December 13, 2026

questions.question: What types of help do Metro State academic advisors provide?
questions.expected_answer: Advisors explain degree requirements, help plan schedules, review the Degree Audit Report, and help students stay on track for graduation.
questions.expected_evidence: Academic advisors help students understand degree requirements, plan course schedules, review their Degree Audit Report (DARs), and stay on track for graduation.
accepted_answers: degree requirements, schedules, degree audit, and graduation planning

questions.question: Where can students receive help with essays and research papers?
questions.expected_answer: The Writing Center helps students with essays, research papers, and other written assignments.
questions.expected_evidence: The Writing Center supports students with essays, research papers, and other written assignments.

questions.question: How much is the technology fee per credit?
questions.expected_answer: The technology fee is $14 per credit.
questions.expected_evidence: Technology Fee: $14 per credit.

questions.question: Which company administers Metro State's tuition payment plan?
questions.expected_answer: The tuition payment plan is offered through Nelnet Campus Commerce.
questions.expected_evidence: Metro State offers a tuition payment plan through Nelnet Campus Commerce.

questions.question: What is the general undergraduate tuition rate per credit for Fall 2025 through Summer 2026?
questions.expected_answer: The general undergraduate tuition rate is $302.84 per credit.
questions.expected_evidence:
GENERAL RATES (Per Credit)
Undergraduate: $302.84

questions.question: At what age can a Minnesota resident normally qualify for senior citizen tuition?
questions.expected_answer: A legal Minnesota resident normally qualifies at age 62 before the start of the term.
questions.expected_evidence:
Must be a legal Minnesota resident.
- Must be 62 years old before the start of the term.

accepted_answers: I don't have enough information in the provided Metro State documents to answer that question.

Monday, October 19, 2026

questions.question: What are the Spring 2026 spring break dates?
questions.expected_answer: Spring 2026 spring break runs from March 8 through March 14, 2026.
questions.expected_evidence:
Sunday–Saturday, March 8–14, 2026
– Spring Break (no classes, offices open)

questions.question: On what dates does Ramadan occur in the 2026 religious observance calendar?
questions.expected_answer: Ramadan begins at sundown February 17 and runs through March 18, 2026.
questions.expected_evidence: Ramadan (Islamic) begins at sundown; February 17–March 18, 2026

questions.question: Which first-year applicants fall into conditional admission based on high school GPA?
questions.expected_answer: First-year applicants with a cumulative high school GPA between 2.5 and 2.75 fall into conditional admission.
questions.expected_evidence: For students with a cumulative GPA between 2.5 and 2.75

questions.question: What GPA and credit conditions qualify a transfer applicant for automatic admission?
questions.expected_answer: Automatic transfer admission requires a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher and at least 16 attempted transferable semester credits.
questions.expected_evidence:
Requires a cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher
   - At least 16 transferable semester credits attempted

questions.question: Which transfer applicants fall into conditional admission based on GPA?
questions.expected_answer: Transfer applicants with a cumulative GPA between 1.5 and 2.0 fall into conditional admission.
questions.expected_evidence: For students with a cumulative GPA between 1.5 and 2.0

questions.question: When must financial-aid loans generally be repaid?
questions.expected_answer: Loans generally must be repaid after graduation or when enrollment drops below half-time.
questions.expected_evidence: Loans: Borrowed funds that must be repaid after graduation or when enrollment drops below half-time.
accepted_answers: after graduation or below half-time enrollment

questions.question: How is financial aid applied, and what happens to funds left afterward?
questions.expected_answer: Aid is first applied to tuition, fees, and other university charges; any remaining funds are refunded to the student.
questions.expected_evidence:
Aid is first applied to tuition, fees, and other university charges
- Any remaining funds are refunded to the student
accepted_answers: charges are paid first and the remainder is refunded

questions.question: What are the opening and closing dates for the Fall 2026 bookstore credit program?
questions.expected_answer: The Fall 2026 bookstore credit program runs from July 20 through August 31, 2026.
questions.expected_evidence:
Monday, July 20, 2026
Fall 2026 bookstore credit program begins
questions.reviewer_notes: The same source later states that the program ends Monday, August 31, 2026.

questions.question: What can happen to unearned federal aid and the student's balance after a Return to Title IV calculation?
questions.expected_answer: Unearned federal aid must be returned to the federal government, and the student may then owe the university a balance.
questions.expected_evidence:
Unearned aid must be returned to the federal government
- Students may owe a balance to the university after the calculation
accepted_answers: unearned aid is returned and the student may owe a balance

questions.question: What GPA range qualifies for Magna Cum Laude, and what Metro State credit minimum also applies?
questions.expected_answer: Magna Cum Laude requires a GPA from 3.800 through 3.899 and at least 30 upper-division graded credits completed at Metro State.
questions.expected_evidence: Magna Cum Laude: GPA 3.800–3.899
questions.reviewer_notes: The next sentence in the same honors section supplies the 30-credit requirement.

questions.question: When and where are diplomas mailed after degree posting?
questions.expected_answer: Diplomas are mailed to the permanent address in eServices approximately 8 to 10 weeks after degree posting.
questions.expected_evidence: Diplomas are mailed to the permanent address listed in eServices approximately 8–10 weeks after degree posting.
accepted_answers: 8–10 weeks after posting to the permanent eServices address

questions.question: Which colleges are assigned to the second Fall 2025 commencement ceremony?
questions.expected_answer: The second ceremony includes the College of Business and Management, College of Individualized Studies, College of Liberal Arts, and School of Urban Education.
questions.expected_evidence:
Second Ceremony (2:30 p.m., doors open 1:45 p.m.)
- College of Business and Management
- College of Individualized Studies
- College of Liberal Arts
- School of Urban Education
accepted_answers: Business and Management, Individualized Studies, Liberal Arts, and Urban Education

questions.question: When may an incomplete grade be granted, and how is the remaining work deadline set?
questions.expected_answer: An incomplete may be granted when most coursework is complete but extenuating circumstances prevent finishing; the instructor sets the deadline for the remaining work.
questions.expected_evidence: An incomplete (“I”) may be granted when a student has completed most coursework but cannot finish due to extenuating circumstances. Students must complete remaining work by the deadline set by the instructor.
accepted_answers: most work completed, extenuating circumstances, instructor deadline

questions.question: What appears on the transcript after a course withdrawal, and what else may it affect?
questions.expected_answer: A withdrawal places a W on the transcript and may affect financial aid.
questions.expected_evidence: A withdrawal results in a “W” on the transcript and may impact financial aid.
accepted_answers: W on the transcript and possible financial aid impact

questions.question: What attendance choices does a HyFlex course provide for each class session?
questions.expected_answer: For each session, students may attend in person, online synchronously, or online asynchronously.
questions.expected_evidence: Students may choose to attend each class session in person, online synchronously, or online asynchronously, depending on their preference.
accepted_answers: in person, online synchronous, or online asynchronous

questions.question: How are students notified about an available waitlist seat, and what determines priority?
questions.expected_answer: Students are notified by email, and priority is based on the order in which they joined the waitlist.
questions.expected_evidence:
Students are notified through email if a seat becomes available.
- Waitlist priority is based on the order students join the list.
accepted_answers: email notification; first joined determines priority

questions.question: What age exception applies to a Minnesota resident receiving a railroad retirement annuity?
questions.expected_answer: A Minnesota resident receiving a railroad retirement annuity may qualify for senior citizen tuition at age 60.
questions.expected_evidence: Individuals receiving a railroad retirement annuity qualify at age 60.

questions.question: What is the listed total per-credit cost for a senior citizen auditing a course?
questions.expected_answer: The listed total is $15.00 per credit, plus any applicable course-specific charges.
questions.expected_evidence: Total Cost: $15.00 per credit (plus any applicable course-specific charges)

questions.question: What is the listed total per-credit cost for a senior citizen taking a course for credit?
questions.expected_answer: The listed total is $58.30 per credit, plus any applicable course-specific charges.
questions.expected_evidence: Total Cost: $58.30 per credit (plus any applicable course-specific charges)

questions.question: How is the tuition payment deadline adjusted for a student with an official financial aid award letter?
questions.expected_answer: The deadline is extended until one week after financial aid is disbursed.
questions.expected_evidence: Students who have received an official financial aid award letter will have their tuition payment deadline extended until one week after financial aid is disbursed.
accepted_answers: one week after aid is disbursed

questions.question: What must a student do if a tuition waiver does not cover the full amount?
questions.expected_answer: The student must pay the remaining balance by the tuition payment deadline.
questions.expected_evidence: If a waiver does not cover the full amount, the student must pay the remaining balance by the tuition payment deadline.
accepted_answers: pay the remaining balance by the deadline

questions.question: Which records must transfer applicants submit besides ordinary college or university transcripts?
questions.expected_answer: They must also submit official records for military credits and CLEP or AP credits, when applicable.
questions.expected_evidence:
Transfer applicants must submit official transcripts from all post-secondary institutions attended, including:
- Colleges or universities where credits were attempted
- Military credits
- CLEP or AP credits
accepted_answers: military credits and CLEP or AP credits
